column2: The more you chase after wealth, the less you sleep. Sleep earns nothing, after all. You lie awake reckoning tolls and tithes and the price of grain, and rise before the cock to check the ledgers again.
I must have more gold!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has often said that the [From.PrimaryTitle.GetTier] of [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName] must find new ways to fill its coffers. Now a chance has come up to open a new and perhaps very profitable trade route.
I will take it to [From.GetTitledFirstName].
I have more important matters to attend to.

Your [steward.GetJobTitle], [steward.GetFirstName], comes to see you one afternoon with a sheaf of maps and figures. [steward.GetSheHeCap] has a plan to bring in exotic goods by opening a trade route with a foreign realm. It would need a great deal of coin to start, but the profits could be greater still.
Let us organise an expedition.
My coin has better uses.
It is time to buy beasts of burden for the caravan. Strong mules and sturdy oxen are to be had at the market, but at a hefty price.
It is time to buy beasts of burden for the caravan. Sure-footed pack ponies bred for the mountain roads are to be had at the hold's market, but the beast-masters know their worth and will not haggle.
Buy them. Only the best will do.
Hire some cut-throats to steal them.
On second thought, this is too dear.
It is time to fit out a ship for the expedition. The harbourmaster shows you a broad-bellied merchantman with a hold that would be perfect for the venture, but it comes at a hefty price.
Buy the ship.
Hire some cut-throats to steal it.
On second thought, this is too dear.

Word of the expedition has spread, and a group of [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s of [Root.Religion.GetName] has come to court with a request. They will put temple funds towards the journey if they may come along and carry the word of their god to foreign lands.
Of course. It will be an honour to have you.
No. I cannot have you getting in the way.

For days the [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s have been giving the crew dark looks, and today they come to you to complain about travelling with thieves and cut-throats. The faithful of [Root.Religion.GetName], they say, should not keep such company.
Oh well.
We are helping these poor souls to an honest life.

A message arrives: [From.GetTitledFirstName] means to open a trade route that will run through waters and markets where our own merchants have long done business. Surely this deserves some compensation.
Demand compensation.
Never mind.

Dear [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I have been told of your plans to trade near my lands. I trust that you mean to compensate the [From.PrimaryTitle.GetFullName] for this intrusion into its markets.

Signed,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Here are some coins for the [From.GetTitle].
This is none of your business.

Dear [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

Of course you shall be compensated for the intrusion.

Signed,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

Dear [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I understand your concerns, but my ventures are none of your business.

Signed,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Excellent!
That pirate!
The cut-throats I hired botched the theft of the pack beasts. Worse, some of them were caught, and under the lash they named me. The expedition will have to be abandoned for now.
The cut-throats I hired botched the theft of the ship. Worse, some of them were caught, and under the lash they named me. The expedition will have to be abandoned for now.
That is terrible!
It is time for the expedition to set out. With luck it will bring back a fine profit.
To foreign lands!
More than a month has passed since the expedition set out, and we have found no one willing to trade with us. The crew are homesick and have turned the company round for home.
Hard luck.
The expedition has reached the realm of [business_partner.GetTitledFirstName] at last. [steward.GetFirstName] asks what gift we should present as a token of friendship.
A dozen strong horses.
A dozen sturdy camels.
A mighty elephant.
A dozen hardy warriors.
A dozen barrels of the finest ale from the hold's oldest brewery.
A chest of fine cloth from home.
A pouch of rare herbs.
My courtesy is gift enough.

At the welcome feast I notice [business_partner.GetBestName]'s face growing red with disgust as [steward.GetFirstName] shovels food into [steward.GetHerHis] mouth with bare hands, as is the custom where we come from.
Explain to our host that [steward.GetSheHe] only follows the customs of our people.
Please excuse [steward.GetHerHim]. I am still teaching this barbarian some manners.
I am hungry too!

Walking idly through the court of [business_partner.GetTitledFirstName], I hear raised voices round a corner. There I find one of the [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s of the expedition locked in a furious theological argument with a local noble. This could ruin the whole venture!
This must stop, now.
I will step in with a jest and calm them both.
These heretics must see the error of their ways.
These heathens must see the error of their ways.
The longer I talk with [business_partner.GetBestName], the more I realise that we share far more than a head for business.
After long hours of haggling over terms, [business_partner.GetBestName] and I have come to an agreement at last.

The talks with [business_partner.GetBestName] grow ever more bitter, until [business_partner.GetSheHe] slams [business_partner.GetHerHis] fist on the table. It seems [business_partner.GetSheHe] cannot bear the sight of me any longer, and as I leave the hall [business_partner.GetSheHe] shouts after me: "Begone, you swindling wretch!"
I have won a friend and a fine bargain.
This will be a profitable agreement.
So that is that.
While at the foreign court I spent some time watching how the courtiers keep their accounts and run their lands. It is fascinating how differently they manage things here.
I should use some of these tricks at home.
With the new trade route open, I return with the first load of goods and sell it at a handsome profit. The flow of new wares will enrich the realm for years to come.
One can never have too much coin.
My [steward.GetJobTitle], [steward.GetFirstName], has brought riches to the realm with [steward.GetHerHis] able handling of the expedition, and [steward.GetSheHe] no doubt expects a share of them.
[steward.GetSheHeCap] will be rewarded as [steward.GetSheHe] deserves.
[steward.GetSheHeCap] was only doing [steward.GetHerHis] duty.
The expedition has failed, and everyone at court knows it.
At least I learned something.
The caravans that run the trade route from [Root.GetName] are worn out. New beasts and gear are needed if the goods are to keep coming.
The ship that runs the trade route from [Root.GetName] is worn out. A new ship and gear are needed if the goods are to keep coming.
The trade route must not fail.
It is too dear.

I have spent countless hours sketching plans for one building or another, when it suddenly comes to me how to show the world my genius as a builder. I will raise a great tower, one that will dwarf everything else for leagues around.

I have spent countless hours sketching plans for one great work or another, when it suddenly comes to me. The ancestors carved their holds deep into the mountains. I will raise a tower above them, a watchtower of stone and runes that will stand for a thousand years and be seen from every peak.
It will be glorious.
But I cannot afford it.
The tower will need a mason to work the stone, for beauty as much as for strength. Who should I hire for such delicate work?
I know a master mason with the skill.
Any boy off the street will do.
Word of my great building has spread through the realm. A few scoff, but most of the burghers are openly impressed by the scale of the tower.
The doubters will be proven wrong.

[stonemason.GetBestName] has been working day and night on how the stones for the tower are to be cut. [stonemason.GetSheHeCap] comes to me now with dark rings under [stonemason.GetHerHis] eyes and asks for more coin, saying [stonemason.GetHerHis] father is sick and the family needs help.

[stonemason.GetBestName] comes to complain about how hard and tiring it is to plan the cutting of the stones, and asks for more pay, since the first is already spent. Strangely, the gossip at court says [stonemason.GetSheHe] has had plenty of time to chase after every pretty face in the castle.
Very well, but keep working.
You are spending the money on your lustful adventures.
Very well, but keep working.
I have already paid you. Now get to work, or else!
Before a building this large can be started, we must be sure of enough good stone. My steward suggests buying it from a trusted trading partner, though a quarry nearby would profit the whole region.
Buy the stone.
Open a quarry.
There are old stones enough in the castle walls.

At the tower site in [Root.Capital.GetName], a rope snapped and a block of granite fell on the workers below, crushing several of them. The people now demand stricter care on the site, and coin for the widows and orphans.
Peasants are cheap.
The families will be paid for their loss.
After decades of giving the county its building stone, the quarry in [Root.GetName] has been closed. Its seams are worked out.
A pity.

[tower_priest.GetBestName] comes to me in a fury. [tower_priest.GetSheHeCap] has seen that my tower now stands taller than any temple in the realm. "This is arrogance!" [tower_priest.GetSheHe] cries. "No stone raised by mortal hands may look down on the house of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]! Do you think to climb up to the gods themselves?"
Go back to your scrolls, priest.
I suppose we can take a few courses off the top.
I only follow the word of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].
[tower_priest.GetSheHeCap] knows too much. [tower_priest.GetSheHeCap] must disappear.
§Y[tower_priest.GetBestName]§! will be lured to the top of the tower...

I have persuaded [tower_priest.GetBestName] to climb with me to the top of the scaffolding, so that [tower_priest.GetSheHe] may see the tower properly. The view from the top is breathtaking, as [tower_priest.GetFirstName] is about to find out.
Careful, now...
[Root.GetFirstName] gives [tower_priest.GetFirstName] a push.

I put all my weight behind my outstretched arms to push [tower_priest.GetBestName] off the tower, and just then [tower_priest.GetSheHe] bends down. [tower_priest.GetSheHeCap] must have spotted a coin. I stumble past [tower_priest.GetHerHim] and out into the empty air.
Oh dear...
As [tower_priest.GetBestName] admires the view from the top of the tower, I reach out and give [tower_priest.GetHerHim] a gentle push.
Oh dear.

The great tower I began so long ago is finished at last. It can be seen from leagues away, and people are as awed as they are frightened by the power such a feat displays. In the years of work I have mastered many secrets of the builder's art, and the tower will hold back many thousands of enemy soldiers.
I am a builder now, in truth.
It was merely a pastime.

My pride, the great tower of [Root.GetName], has begun to lean. People everywhere snigger behind my back and trade rude jokes about it. The only thing greater than my shame is my fear that it will fall.
Before I held the county of [Root.GetName], a great tower was raised here by [tower_founder.GetBestName]. Now, after years of standing proud, it has begun to lean, and people fear it will fall.
This is all the mason's fault!
Lazy workers who could not follow instructions!
It is my own fault, I am afraid.
How unfortunate. It is a fine tower.
The tower leans further every day. Perhaps I should try to save it by propping it up?
I must save the tower whatever it costs!
A reasonable effort will do.
I will leave it to fate.
The tower has been shored up and has stopped tipping. It rests at a steady angle now, and I hope it will stay that way. It still leans badly, though, and I am embarrassed to admit that I built it.
The tower has been shored up and has stopped tipping. It rests at a steady angle now, and I hope it will stay that way. It still leans badly, though, and it looks very strange.
At least it did not fall on anyone's head.

I wake in the middle of the night to a great crack, then a long rumbling like the loudest thunder I have ever heard. I rush to the window, fearing the worst, and I am right. The leaning tower has fallen at last, and thousands of blocks of stone have come down on the houses below.
I hope no one was hurt.

Word comes that a famous statesman from a far land has arrived in my realm, and I ride out to greet the party myself. Before I can even begin the courtesies, the visitor points at the leaning tower and cries: "Where is [tower_founder.GetBestName], the magnificent mind behind this masterpiece? I would pay handsomely to meet this genius!"

Word comes that a famous statesman from a far land has arrived in my realm, and I ride out to greet the party myself. Before I can even begin the courtesies, the visitor points at the leaning tower and cries: "Where is [tower_founder.GetBestName], the magnificent mind behind this masterpiece? The slanted door, the uneven stairs... such daring! I would pay handsomely to meet this genius!"

Word comes that a famous statesman from a far land has arrived in my realm, and I ride out to greet the party myself. Before I can even begin the courtesies, the visitor points at the leaning tower and cries: "Where is [stonemason.GetBestName], the magnificent mind behind this masterpiece? I would pay handsomely to meet this genius!"

Word comes that a famous statesman from a far land has arrived in my realm, and I ride out to greet the party myself. Before I can even begin the courtesies, the visitor points at the leaning tower and cries: "Where is [stonemason.GetBestName], the magnificent mind behind this masterpiece? The slanted door, the uneven stairs... such daring! I would pay handsomely to meet this genius!"
Ahem. Of course, I will fetch [stonemason.GetHerHim] from my, ah... court.
I will fetch [stonemason.GetHerHim] at once.
[stonemason.GetSheHeCap] is not here. [stonemason.GetSheHeCap] has more important matters to attend to.
You are speaking to [Root.GetHerHim] right now.
It was built before my time.
Ahem. Of course, I will fetch [stonemason.GetHerHim] from my, ah... court.
[stonemason.GetSheHeCap] is not here. [stonemason.GetSheHeCap] has more important matters to attend to.

Greeting the sun from my window one morning, I notice for the first time how the castle garden has been left to rot for years. The weeds are knee-high and the brambles so thick that no one could pass without a sword. Something must be done.
I will make it a true garden, with a glorious hedge maze!
But there is so little time.
Clearing the weeds from a garden this size is hard work. It will take many days of toil before the hedges for the maze can even be planted.
I will do it myself.
I will find someone to help me.
The servants could use more work.
The hedges are planted, and while they grow I turn to the other things my garden needs. Should there be statues at the dead ends of the maze?
Magnificent statues of my family.
Statues of the ancestors of my clan, carved by the finest masons of the hold.
Statues of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] and the heroes of the faith.
The shadows are decoration enough.
Your §YDynasty§! will appreciate the gesture.\n
Every self-respecting garden has a fountain, someone once told me. Here is my chance to build one, and to show off a little.
A great fountain in the middle.
A fountain that flows with wine every day of the week.
A fountain that flows with ale every day of the week.
It is not worth the coin.
It is time to fill the beds round the garden. I could bring in rare blooms from far away, from the gardens of Tilea and the hothouses of Marienburg, or plant the flowers of the local meadows.
Bring in rare blooms from afar.
Our own flowers are as fair as any.
There is an unused spot in a quiet corner of the garden. Some would say it is the perfect place for a cosy pavilion.
How romantic. Build it.
A bit too romantic for my taste.

The hedge maze and the garden are finished at last. The costly touches I added have not gone unnoticed, and the garden's beauty is famous far beyond my realm. In making it I have learned much about how to make things grow and flourish, flowers and friendships alike.

The hedge maze and the garden are finished at last. A maze this intricate is sure to be talked of across the realm. In making it I have learned much about how to make things grow and flourish, flowers and friendships alike.
I like to see things flourish.
I am not ready to give my life to gardening...

A group of carpenters in [business_province.GetName] have begun working together and taking on apprentices of their own. This cannot be ignored. I can approve their guild and win the good will of the craftsmen, or outlaw it before it chokes the local market.
I will support the carpenters.
Outlaw the guild.

A master minter has offered his services. If I wish, he will strike new coin for the realm, finely made and stamped with a splendid likeness of my face, so that every peasant who pays a toll is reminded who rules here.
Strike true coin, for my glory.
Thin the silver with base metal, for profit.
We have coin enough.
A merchant has found that my new coins are debased, with far less silver in them than they should hold. The whole realm is calling me a cheat and a skinflint.
Now people will spit on my face on those coins.
[business_burgher.GetTitledFirstName] asks to buy a plot of my land in [Root.Capital.GetName]. It is a hard choice, for [business_burgher.GetSheHe] offers to pay well for it.
I do need the gold...
There is not enough gold in your purse to buy my land.

A group of craftsmen from [business_province.GetName] have come to court to show me their work. Their wares are fine, and I am sure they would sell well in the realm. Seeing my interest, they ask me for the coin to set up a workshop, since they cannot raise it themselves.
A sound investment.
Your lack of coin is not my problem.
A workshop will be set up in [business_province.GetName] and begin making goods.

The craftsmen I backed two years ago have come to tell me of their success. With my coin they set up their workshop, and it is now one of the most profitable businesses in [business_province.GetName].
Excellent! More taxes for me.

There is a faint knock at my door, and a small figure peeks in. I remember him well: one of the craftsmen I backed two years ago. Shamefaced, he tells me that the business did not go as planned, and the workshop has gone under with nothing to show for it.
That was a bad investment...
Ever since I took up the pursuit of wealth and began to keep a close eye on income and spending, my coffers have been full more often than not.
A thriving trade makes a thriving realm.
